criteria.criterion: The change description names the root cause: the planner brief gives no computed list of existing callers or exits for the functions in the deliverable files, only prose, so plans skipped adjacent paths such as `[parallel] max_concurrency` into landing. Checked in the diff of CHANGELOG.md and the doc comment on the new code in crates/athena-context/src/briefs/planner.rs.
criteria.evidence: The new CHANGELOG bullet says: 'the planner brief gave no computed list of existing callers or exits for the functions in the deliverable files, only prose rules (OPEN_QUESTION_RULE, CODE_CLAIMS_RULE) ... so plans skipped adjacent paths such as `[parallel] max_concurrency` into landing'. The doc comments on CallSite, DeliverableFact.callers and EXITS_RULE in planner.rs, and on deliverable_facts in planning.rs, give the same cause. They cite the four jobs and say this is information, not a refusal.

criteria.criterion: DeliverableFact in crates/athena-context/src/briefs/planner.rs gains a callers field. A unit test in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs builds a planner brief and asserts that each caller (file:line) appears in the deliverables section. Run: cargo test -p athena-context.
criteria.evidence: `pub callers: Option<CallerList>` was added to DeliverableFact, and planner_brief now calls callers_section. The test a_planner_brief_lists_the_callers_of_each_deliverable takes the text between the Deliverables heading and the next heading. It asserts that crates/b/src/y.rs:20, crates/c/src/z.rs:7, crates/d/src/w.rs:3 and 'crates/b/tests/it.rs:9 (test)' appear there, and that none of them appear after '## Report'. Both tests passed (2 passed). Athena's fails-without-2 run showed the tests do not compile without the fix.

criteria.criterion: A test in crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs or run/tests.rs computes callers from a fixture snapshot where a function in a deliverable file has callers in two other files. It asserts both are listed, and that a deliverable with no callers is shown as such, not omitted. It fails without the change. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: The test deliverable_callers_lists_both_callers_and_shows_a_deliverable_with_none builds a real git repository and asserts that land_job's call sites are exactly [a.rs:2, b.rs:3, tests/it.rs:1 (test)]. It also asserts that other.rs's `lonely` is present with 0/0 callers. deliverable_callers_reach_the_planner_prompt checks that the real planner prompt contains a.rs:2, b.rs:3 and 'No callers found: `quiet_one` (line 1), `quiet_two` (line 2)'. All 12 tests matching the filter passed (9 new). Athena's fails-without-3 run showed they do not compile without the fix (deliverable_facts and callers_of are missing).

criteria.criterion: A new exits rule const in crates/athena-context/src/briefs/planner.rs is added to the planner Report. It requires a plan that changes a stage or core flow to tabulate every exit (success, fail, error, hold, interrupt) with the file:line that handles it. A test in briefs.rs asserts that wording appears exactly once, in a first-round brief and in a revision brief.
criteria.evidence: EXITS_RULE is added at the end of the shared Report format string, so both first-round and revision briefs include it. Its text: 'A plan that adds or changes a stage or core flow must tabulate every exit of each new or changed stage (success, fail, error, hold, interrupt): for each exit, the file:line that handles it...'. The test the_planner_brief_requires_an_exit_table_once_in_both_rounds asserts the rule appears exactly once after '## Report' in both briefs; it passed. The Report size bound test was updated to count the new rule.

criteria.criterion: No refusal rule is added. admission.rs and the reading checks are unchanged, so expected 0% of newly refused readings.
criteria.evidence: The diff stat for admission.rs, reading.rs and tests/refusal_corpus.rs is empty. The new code only adds information to the brief; no check reads DeliverableFact.callers or EXITS_RULE. Athena's replay of past readings found 0 of 50 accepted readings newly refused.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the change.
criteria.evidence: There is one new bullet at the top of '### Changed' under Unreleased. It covers the root cause, the three code changes, the limits (search by name only, cost not measured, effect on planning not measured), that 0% of readings are newly refused, and the test filters.

findings.summary: Scope: crates/athena-core/src/code_health.rs is changed but is not on the expected deliverables list.
findings.evidence: is_cfg_test and is_test_fn changed from private to pub(crate), and doc comments were added, so the caller scan uses the same definition of test code. The change was in the planned files and the CHANGELOG mentions it. It only changes visibility and alters no behavior.

findings.summary: Every planner round re-reads and re-parses every Rust file in the base commit; the time and memory this takes was not measured.
findings.evidence: planning_round calls deliverable_facts on every round, including revisions. Each call runs ls_tree plus cat_blobs in chunks of 200 and a syn parse of every .rs file. The CHANGELOG says this cost was not measured and estimates it at a few seconds. Reading the files once per job, or once per base commit, would avoid repeating the work. The design is sound otherwise: it parses the code properly rather than matching text, and the brief says the results are approximate.

findings.summary: Calls are matched by name only, so common names such as `new` or `run` will list many false callers.
findings.evidence: The index is keyed only on the identifier at the end of the call. The brief says a same-named method of another type gives a false hit, and the output is capped, so the brief cannot grow without limit. Nothing refuses work based on this list.

summary: The change fixes the problem where it starts: what the planner is given. Before planning, Athena now parses every Rust file in the base commit and finds who calls each function declared in each existing Rust deliverable. The planner brief lists those callers by file:line, with a label saying the list is approximate and only a starting point. The brief's Report section also gains one new rule, EXITS_RULE: a plan that changes a stage must give a table of every exit (success, fail, error, hold, interrupt) with the file:line that handles it. No refusal rule was added, and admission.rs, reading.rs and the refusal corpus are unchanged. I ran the three planned test filters: athena-context `callers` (2 passed), athena-context `exit_table` (1 passed) and athena-core `caller` (12 passed, 9 of them new; the other 3 only match the filter by name). The 9 new tests include a test against a real git repository where one function has callers in two other files and a deliverable with no callers is still shown, plus a test that runs the actual planner prompt. Athena's earlier runs showed these tests fail to compile once the fix is taken out. The CHANGELOG entry and the doc comments name the root cause. fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in CI. There are no blocker or major findings. Two minor ones: code_health.rs is changed even though it is not on the deliverables list (planned, visibility only), and every planner round re-reads all Rust files in the repository, a cost that was not measured.
